receipt.public_excerpt: The Department of War has stated they will only contract with AI companies who accede to “any lawful use” and remove safeguards in the cases mentioned above. evidence_items.explanation: The demand was 'any lawful use' plus removing the mass-surveillance and autonomous-weapons safeguards, backed by three serious threats. This is the party on the receiving end describing the demand.

receipt.public_excerpt: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth gave Anthropic's CEO a Friday deadline to open the company's artificial intelligence technology for unrestricted military use or risk losing its government contract

evidence_items.explanation: Independent wire report that Hegseth personally set a deadline for 'unrestricted military use' and tied it to threats.

receipt.public_excerpt: The Pentagon has given Anthropic until 5:01 p.m. Friday to drop its objections to using Claude in relation to autonomous weapons and mass surveillance of U.S. citizens.

evidence_items.explanation: Confirms the demand specifically targeted Anthropic's objections on autonomous weapons and surveillance.

receipt.public_excerpt: the department had no interest in conducting mass domestic surveillance nor deploying autonomous weapons, but wanted to use AI for “all lawful purposes.”

evidence_items.explanation: The Pentagon denied wanting these uses and framed its demand as bounded by law. This cuts against the 'for applications such as' framing, though not against the demand itself.
